description: Classifies skill lifecycle eligibility and selects the deterministic canonical routing owner. Use when records overlap, a candidate competes with a current skill, aliases collide, or archived and quarantined sources must be excluded.
intent_owner: Lifecycle eligibility and routing priority application
intent: Apply the lifecycle and priority contract to a bounded set of capability records.
outcome: Select at most one eligible canonical owner or return an explicit collision or ineligibility result.
non_goals: Discover authority from folder or alphabetical order
inputs: Explicit sandbox or legacy invocation context

permissions.allowed_scope: Read declared capability records and emit a decision receipt

positive: prove a candidate cannot outrank current
resolve an alias or archive routing collision

lifecycle.promotion_gate: Adversarial lifecycle and collision tests plus lifecycle-authority owner approval

instructions: Validate required lifecycle fields and fail closed when more than one current-authorized record owns the same intent, scope, and surface.
Exclude archived-retained, quarantined-untrusted, rejected, unavailable, unauthorized, and wrong-surface records before ranking.
Prefer an exact explicit current-authorized owner, then a matching authorized project or domain owner, then the current cross-platform canonical owner.
Admit candidate-sandbox only in an explicit evaluation sandbox and keep it below a matching current owner regardless of numeric priority.
Admit a compatibility-alias only for a legacy invocation the successor cannot satisfy.
Within one eligible class prefer higher specificity, then fresher evidence, then lower context and tool cost; use stable ID only as a deterministic final tie break.
Return the selected owner and exclusions as a receipt without changing lifecycle state or activation.
